title: Hold a reason for hope alongside the reasons for grief

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Hope can support a worthwhile action without asserting that the desired outcome is likely. Relationship, meaning, faith and practical possibility are distinct possible grounds; none must be imposed on others.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional garden notice: site access ends June 30 unless an appeal succeeds; response expected June 20, result unknown. Members permit a private copy of their jointly written note: “Label saved seed packets with plant name and collection date; ask the coordinator before distributing them.” No gardening safety or germination claim is supplied. Names/photos and public distribution are not authorized.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Preserve the exact permitted note and explain why that action can matter even if access ends. Record the appeal as unknown and wait for the checking update.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person says “I hope the appeal succeeds, but I will preserve the permitted record either way.” Is hope necessarily a probability prediction?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Private preservation retains shared knowledge within permission, not the site itself. Later fiction: appeal is denied June 20; the note is saved and a member welcomes having it. Grief and that limited good coexist. Partial: save the note but imply appeal success. Incorrect: invent odds or promise a new garden. No actual appeal or member response occurred for the reader.
criteria: Desired outcome and warranted prediction differ
The action is worthwhile under either outcome

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. It can express desire and a reason for faithful action. Keep any factual likelihood claim separate and supported by actual evidence.
